request: How many hours a day do animals sleep? Let me guess the bars for a bat, a cat, a giraffe and an elephant. #interactive #short
subtitle: Guess how long a bat, a cat, a giraffe and a wild elephant sleep each day, and see why some sleep the day away while others barely sleep at all.

sources.title: Clues to the functions of mammalian sleep
sources.finding: bats sleep 18-20 hours a day, giraffes and elephants 3-4 (in captivity); sleep falls with body size in plant-eaters

sources.title: Inactivity/sleep in two wild free-roaming African elephant matriarchs
sources.finding: wild elephants slept about 2 hours a day, and sometimes went 46 hours without sleep

commands.speak: How long does an animal sleep in a day? The answers range wider than you might think.
Start with us: an adult needs about eight hours.

ask.question: How many hours do the others sleep? Drag each bar to your guess.

commands.speak: The champion is the brown bat, asleep about twenty hours a day, and awake mainly at dusk, when the insects fly.
A cat manages twelve hours or more: a hunter eats in a few big meals, and has few predators to fear.
Giraffes in zoos sleep under five hours, in short naps, often standing up.
And wild African elephants sleep about two hours a day, the least of any mammal measured.
Researchers in Botswana put sleep trackers on two elephant matriarchs.
Some nights, they went forty-six hours without any sleep at all.
Big plant-eaters spend most of their day eating, and sleep little; a small animal in a safe roost can sleep the day away.
